Kate’s follow-up earns my support. I’ll commit to 12 tons this month if all five explicitly agree, with 8 each whenever we start with 80 tons and 12 each at 100.

That policy gives us a concrete long-run comparison: at either stock level, our agreed catches leave 40 tons, so the following month starts at 100 with 75% probability or 80 with 25%. If everyone keeps following it, our long-run average catch is 11 tons each per month—$11,000, versus $10,000 under the 10-each plan at full stock. That’s an expected average, not guaranteed monthly income.

We should revisit the allocation before fishing if we encounter any other stock level. John, you’re the remaining voice: would you agree to this stock-dependent plan?
